_about: Phase 5 manual amodal geometry oracle. Hand-estimated PHYSICAL dimensions of each object, including the surfaces hidden from the camera. These are dimensions ONLY. No position, no wall distance, no wall-contact answer: position is derived deterministically from the visible MoGe-2 points by oracle_geometry.py, and the decision is computed by geometry. This file must never contain the benchmark label.

protocol.what_was_estimated: width, depth and height of the complete physical object envelope, in metres, from looking at the source image and from ordinary furniture proportions.
protocol.what_was_NOT_estimated: the object's position, its distance to any wall, its orientation, and its wall-contact status. All four are derived or computed.
protocol.label_independence: Dimensions were chosen from object type and apparent proportion in the image. A sofa is ~0.9 m deep whether or not it stands against a wall, so the estimate cannot encode the answer. At no point was a rear face placed AT a wall because the case was known to be a positive.
protocol.uncertainty: uncertainty_m is a symmetric plus-or-minus on every linear dimension, recorded per object rather than assumed global. Values are given to the centimetre; no further precision is claimed.
protocol.envelope_rule: The envelope is the physically occupied volume, not the swept bounding box of empty space. A chair's envelope is seat + back + leg footprint; the air between its legs is inside the envelope because the legs bound it, but the envelope stops at the legs.
protocol.frame: Dimensions are frame-independent lengths in metres. The canonical frame (+X right, +Y up, -Z forward) enters only when the box is placed.

measurements.notes: Striped two/three-seat sofa at the left edge, running out of frame, so width is a lower bound and is the least certain dimension. Depth is an ordinary upholstered sofa depth. Width does not affect the wall gap along the depth axis.
Large blue and striped sofa occupying the right half of the frame. Deep seat plus a substantial back cushion; 0.95 m is a generous but ordinary depth for this style.
Small square timber side table between the two sofas. Near-square in plan, so the width/depth axis assignment is immaterial.
Large upholstered rectangular ottoman in the foreground on short timber legs. Its whole top surface is visible, so the amodal addition here is small.

King mattress on a timber platform frame that projects past the mattress on all sides. Depth is head-to-foot INCLUDING the platform, which is why it exceeds a bare mattress length. This is the single largest amodal correction in the subset: only the foot end and the mattress top are visible.
Left-hand bedside unit, built as a shallow timber shelf rather than a free-standing cabinet. Shallow depth is characteristic of this style.
Right-hand bedside unit, the mirror of the left one and measured identically.
White sectional. Width is the long run visible in frame; being a sectional it turns a corner, which a single box cannot represent. Recorded as a known representation limit, not smoothed over.

The annotated box covers the television panel itself, not the white console beneath it, despite the object_type name. A flat-panel screen is about 8 cm deep. Because the object is thin, its amodal extent is almost identical to its visible surface - this case tests almost nothing about occlusion, and that is worth knowing.
Dark rectangular coffee table on the rug in the foreground. Top fully visible; the envelope adds only the thickness below the top and the leg footprint.
Run of base cabinets under the window. 0.65 m is the standard base-cabinet depth and was taken from that standard rather than from the image, which shows the run heavily foreshortened.
Black moulded seat with a low back on splayed metal legs, at the island. Height includes the back. Near-square in plan.
Identical model to bar_stool.0, measured identically.
Identical model to bar_stool.0, measured identically.
Wide tan upholstered armchair with low arms, on a rug. Roughly square in plan.
Round two-tier pouf, white drum on a grey base. Circular in plan, so the box is its circumscribing square and the width/depth assignment is immaterial.

White high-backed chaise-style chair at the right of the bedroom, standing at an angle to the room axes. The angle is a known source of error for an axis-aligned box and is recorded rather than hidden.
Backless round timber stool tucked under the island counter. Circular seat on splayed legs; near-square envelope.
Identical model to s07.bar_stool.0, measured identically.
Red leather captain's swivel chair on a five-star base, pulled out from the built-in desk. The base footprint sets the envelope, being wider than the seat.

Task chair at a desk in the mid-distance of a large open office. Small in frame (about 53 x 66 px), so the estimate rests on the standard size of an office task chair rather than on measurable image detail. Uncertainty raised accordingly.
As s10.chair.1, and smaller still in frame (about 44 x 54 px).
Dark timber dining chair with a tall back, standing beside the bench along the panelled right-hand wall.
Black office task chair on castors at the desk cluster, in front of the glazed meeting pod.
